A zero-shot classifier's softmax gives 0.95 confidence but only 60% of such predictions are correct. What does this show?
options: The scores are not calibrated probabilities.
The text encoder is too large, so its confidences are inflated for each class.
The temperature must be exactly zero for the softmax to be a probability.
The classes are balanced, so a confidence above 0.5 should always be right.
questions.explanation: Softmax of scaled cosines is a score, not a calibrated frequency.

A forced-choice relation test (true vs swapped caption) gives 52 correct of 100. Best interpretation?
options: Consistent with chance; no evidence of grounding.
questions.explanation: SD of a fair-coin count is 5, so 52 is 0.4 SD from 50.

questions.prompt: Which control best shows that an apparent grounding success is not just a language prior?
options: Increase the number of text tokens in each question to add more context.
Use a larger temperature so that the answers depend less on the text.
Report only the best prompt, since it shows the highest grounding accuracy.
Run the same questions with the image blanked or shuffled and compare.
questions.explanation: A text-only baseline exposes priors such as 'cups are usually left of plates'.

questions.prompt: Prompt A: 'a photo of a {c}' scores 62%, prompt B tuned on the test set scores 71%. What is the main issue with preferring B?
options: B was selected on the same data it is evaluated on, so the 71% is optimistic.
A is a photo prompt, so its 62% cannot be compared with another prompt.
B is a longer prompt, and longer prompts always generalise worse than short ones.
Accuracy cannot compare prompts, because the prompts change the label set.
questions.explanation: Selection on the test set inflates the estimate; use validation then test.
